digest.headline: Claude‑BugHunter’s star surge outpaces its 10‑day streak, eclipsing even long‑running superpowers
digest.digest:
The most eye‑catching shift this week is the explosive jump in daily stars for elementalsouls/Claude‑BugHunter, which logged 2,322 stars/day—a ten‑fold increase over its previous peak and the highest ever recorded for any repo in the dataset. The repo, a comprehensive Claude Code skill bundle for security‑focused bug hunting, has now been trending for seven consecutive days after a brief dip last week, suggesting a viral moment likely triggered by a recent security conference demo that showcased its capabilities against real‑world codebases.

Obra/superpowers continues to dominate the developer‑tools conversation, not because it just appeared but because it has amassed a cumulative 91 days in trending, the longest run of any repo. This week it added another six days, driven by the release of version 2.3, which introduces native support for VS Code extensions and a new "agent‑first" workflow that directly competes with the emerging t3code GUI from pingdotgg. Both repos are solving the same problem—streamlining AI‑assisted coding—but superpowers leans into a full‑stack workflow while t3code offers a lightweight web interface.

In the AI/ML arena, Google‑Research/paper‑orchestra made a debut with 1,529 stars/day, a rare all‑time high for a newly‑trending repo. Its multi‑agent framework automates end‑to‑end AI research pipelines, filling a gap left by older tools like NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator, which, despite a solid 953 stars/day, remains a niche validator for agent skills. The contrast highlights a shift from validation toward orchestration, likely spurred by the recent AI research summit where paper‑orchestra was demonstrated.

Finally, the infrastructure sector shows a surprising resurgence: nginx/nginx and openvinotoolkit/openvino both posted velocity jumps of over 12× their prior peaks, reaching 246 and 246 stars/day respectively. Their spikes coincide with the announcement of major version releases—NGINX 1.27 with built‑in HTTP/3 support and OpenVINO 2026.2 with expanded GPU acceleration—suggesting that even mature, stable projects can generate fresh excitement when they deliver substantial feature upgrades.
